text:
kevin: FYI -- Tokyo edge region had a transient GPU capacity degradation earlier, traffic shifted automatically to nearby regions, and most user requests succeeded but latency spiked. Incident is closed but we should update the runbook and follow up with tuning.

infra-bot: Incident #INC-2026-332 created at 2026-03-12T11:12:01Z - region: ap-northeast-1 (tokyo). Auto-failover engaged (route-priority).

kevin: Quick summary: around 11:10 UTC we hit a batch of provisioning timeouts from our edge pool (OOM on provisioning host + slow PV attach), autoscaler pulled new nodes but hit quota throttling for a ~6m window. Traffic split moved ~60% to se-asia and sfo, which kept service up. No customer data loss.

sophia: Can you paste the `kubectl` errors? I saw some attach errors in logs.

kevin: Logs (trimmed):
```
E032 11:09:58  kubelet.go:123] failed to attach volume "pv-attach" for pod token-inference-12: rpc error: code = DeadlineExceeded desc = AttachVolume timeout
W032 11:10:03  quota.go:87] quota request "gpu-ondemand" denied: regional quotaExceeded
```

ajay: Two quick candidate fixes: 1) increase regional burst quota request to cloud (we already have a ticket but need to escalate). 2) pre-warm smaller `edge-prep` instances with empty docker image so PV attach is done earlier.

maria: Adding to runbook: explicit check for `quotaExceeded` in provisioning step, and abort-to-fallback earlier (reduce wait from 30s to 8s). Also add a note to check PV attach latency metric > 2s.

olivia: Agreed. Also we should lower the autoscaler target GPU utilization a bit for edge pools so we have headroom: `target_gpu_util` from 0.75 -> 0.65. That will cost more but reduce this bleedover risk.

ops-sre: Cost ppl FYI: projected ~12% extra monthly GPU spend if we keep lower target across all edge pools. But we can scope to high-risk regions first (tokyo, sfo).

kevin: Proposed immediate runbook edits (actionable):
- Precondition check: `cloud.quota.gpu.available >= requested+buffer(2)` before provisioning. If false -> escalate and route to fallback region immediately.
- PV attach step: if `attach()` doesn't succeed within 8s, mark node as unhealthy and skip to next.
- Autoscaler tuning: edge pools `min_nodes: 4`, `target_gpu_util: 0.65` and `burst_candidate: true`.
- Traffic policy: reduce per-region failover ramp to 30s with gradual 10% increments to avoid sudden capacity shifts.

sophia: I'll draft the PR to the runbook and the k8s operator patch tonight. Assigning myself.

ajay: I'll open a high-priority quota request with cloud support and link it to the incident ticket.

maria: I'll add the PV attach metric and an alert (alert if p95 attach_time > 2s for 5m) and a dashboard panel for it.

olivia: Ops/finance -- tagging @ops-sre for decision on whether to make `target_gpu_util` permanent or scoped.

ops-sre: We prefer scoped approach. Approve lower target for tokyo and sfo for 30 days, then revisit with cost/latency report.

kevin: Post-incident action items (owner -> ETA):
- sophia -> PR: runbook + operator patch (ETA: 2026-03-14)
- ajay -> quota escalation + cloud ticket (ETA: 2026-03-13)
- maria -> metrics + alert + dashboard (ETA: 2026-03-13)
- olivia -> cost impact summary and approval note for scoped tuning (ETA: 2026-03-15)
- kevin -> coordinate failover sim and run weekly smoke for 2 weeks (ETA: start 2026-03-16)

maria: I'll also add a table to runbook with suggested thresholds per region (tokyo: min_nodes 4, target_gpu_util 0.65, ramp_seconds 30).

kevin: One more operational tweak: add a quick `kubectl run` style probe in our rollout job to validate PV attach before accepting routing back to region. Something like:
```bash
kubectl create job pv-attach-check -n infra --image=alpine -- /bin/sh -c "sleep 1; ls /mnt/test || exit 1"
```
If that job fails twice in a row, mark region degraded in the control plane.

infra-bot: Incident #INC-2026-332 status changed -> action_items_assigned.

olivia: Note for postmortem: call out human-in-the-loop decision points (we should avoid manual global traffic changes unless SLA at risk). Also add runbook section for cost-vs-availability tradeoffs and who signs off.

kevin: Agreed. I'll collect the timeline and produce a short postmortem doc after the PRs land. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

sophia: Quick follow-up Q: do we want to add a periodic prewarm job for edge pools at 3am local to keep PV caches warmer?

ajay: That sounds cheap compared to customer latency. I support a scoped prewarm in tokyo and sfo. I'll prototype.

kevin: Great. Closing thread once PRs are open. Keep updates here.
